name: IdempotentConsumer
purpose: Applies a message's effect at most once per logical key while tolerating at-least-once delivery from the transport.
api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Any

class IdempotentConsumer(Protocol):
    def key_for(self, message: Any) -> str: ...
    def handle(self, message: Any) -> None: ...
    def on_duplicate(self, message: Any) -> None: ...
invariants: Two messages with the same idempotency key MUST produce the same observable system state; divergence is FORBIDDEN.
handle CANNOT perform non-compensatable side-effects without first consulting an InboxDeduplicator or equivalent.
on_duplicate MUST NEVER raise as a primary error path; duplicates are an expected steady-state condition.
The consumer SHALL publish its own outputs through a TransactionalOutbox so downstream systems can dedupe similarly.
extension_contract: New consumer types extend IdempotentConsumer by subclassing, overriding key_for and handle, and registering the consumer with the bus via register; pre- and post-processing plug in via middleware while the idempotency contract SHALL remain intact.

sources.locator: Chapter 11, Fault-tolerance of stream processing, pp. 476-479

why_essential: Without a shared contract, every consumer reimplements idempotency differently, and the one that gets it wrong quietly double-charges, double-emails, or double-ships.
alternatives_considered: Exactly-once transport: not achievable end-to-end; only 'effectively-once' under specific conditions.
Manual ad-hoc dedupe per tool: inconsistent and fragile.
Pure upsert operations: ignores effectful consumers (email, payment, webhook).
